Nora Li: FYI - Bluewater ramped production embeddings yesterday, saw a sharp cost jump overnight. Need a short mitigation plan for the QBR and a one-paragraph customer note. cc @Diego
Diego Ramos: Pulling numbers. 24h burn = $9.6k, projected 30d if unchanged = $288k (they usually run ~ $60k/mo). Retainer = $20k/mo, expire in 12 days. :grimacing:
Priya Singh: Is this mostly the indexer or inference? If indexer (bulk writes) vs live queries we have different levers.
Diego Ramos: Breakdown: indexing (long-run batch embeddings) = 58%, query-time similarity = 30%, other = 12%. Indexing spikes due to an aggressive reindex job they enabled.
Nora Li: They turned on parallel indexing to speed onboarding. We recommended staged indexing but they hit full concurrency. Customer wants faster ingestion.
Priya Singh: Quick mitigations we can include in the QBR: (1) pause background indexing (toggle) (2) switch indexer model -> cheaper quantized variant + lower precision (3) enable async batching for query path.
Nora Li: Also need a short auto-throttle policy we can apply account-wide if spend > threshold. Keep it simple for the slide.
Diego Ramos: Draft auto-throttle example for the slide: ```yaml
policy: account_budget_safety
soft_threshold: 30000
hard_threshold: 45000
soft_action: notify-cs+warn-customer
hard_action: pause-indexing+fallback-query-model
```
Priya Singh: Ops note: fallback-query-model = open-sim-compact-4bit, expected query latency +20ms on median, cost -50% per token for query path. Indexing fallback + batch size tuning expected to cut indexing cost by ~60% if we lower concurrency from 12 -> 3.
acct-bot: Account BLUEWTR: credits remaining = $18,200, monthly retainer = $20,000, retainer_expiry = 2026-03-26, auto_renew = false.
notify-bot: ALERT: BLUEWTR has crossed 65% of credits at 1743338800. Owner notified.
Nora Li: For the QBR slide: 1) timeline of what happened (one-liner), 2) immediate steps taken (pause candidate + alert), 3) recommended CTAs (enablement session, staged indexing plan, commit ask). Also capture their priority: faster ingestion > cost for now, but want predictability.
Diego Ramos: Forecast scenarios (30d): status_quo = $288k, throttle+quantize = $140k, staged_index_pause = $72k. Notes: staged pause reduces functionality temporarily.
Priya Singh: I'll prepare the short CLI playbook for ops rollback/rollback and the one-click toggle snippet for customers during enablement: ```bash
# pause indexing jobs
rwctl jobs pause --account BLUEWTR --job indexer-main
# reduce concurrency
rwctl jobs update --account BLUEWTR --job indexer-main --concurrency 3
# swap query model
rwctl accounts set-model --account BLUEWTR --route query --model open-sim-compact-4bit
```
Nora Li: Good. Diego, can you paste the 3 numbers into the QBR slide and add a tiny sparkline for runway? Priya, please write a 2-sentence enablement offer: 30m workshop + config changes + 10-day monitoring window.
Diego Ramos: Uploaded numbers and a simple sparkline image link: https://s.redwood.internal/qbr/bluewtr-spark.png
Priya Singh: Draft enablement blurb: "30-minute ingest & cost optimization workshop: we’ll review indexing concurrency, enable batching and model fallbacks, and implement quick toggles. Includes 10-day monitoring and one rollback assist."
Nora Li: Action items: Diego - finalize numbers and attach to QBR deck by EOD. Priya - prepare the enablement invite and a short checklist. I'll draft the customer note framing this as predictability + temporary measures. Meeting to finalize at 15:30.
Diego Ramos: Will do.
Priya Singh: Prep checklist ready, will share in thread.
notify-bot: Reminder: QBR prep for BLUEWTR scheduled 2026-03-24T15:30:00Z.
